name: @acc/unit-symbol-picker
description: A compact APP-6D / MIL-STD-2525D unit symbol picker: the symbol in the middle, the SIDC above it, a dropdown per position below. Renders through milsymbol.
//files: schemas/ is the JointMilSyML XML everything in src/core/generated is derived from — ~2 MB, which is nothing next to what it settles, and it makes the tarball self-contained: a consumer can re-run scripts/generate-tables.mjs and check the tables against the standard rather than trusting them. src is shipped for the same reason as the sibling packages: the .js.map and .d.ts.map files reference ../src/*.
//exports: ./tables is the generated symbology data, opt-in so the parser entry stays small. ./tables/* reaches one symbol set without the barrel that pulls all 24 — the subpath is the only way a consumer can get tree-shaking here, since a barrel re-export defeats it for most bundlers.
//scripts: generate is deliberately NOT part of build. src/core/generated is committed, so a diff shows exactly what changed when the symbology data is updated, and the build stays a plain tsc with nothing to go wrong in CI. Run it by hand after touching schemas/; the coherence test will fail if the two drift.
//peerDependencies: milsymbol is a hard peer: this package's whole job is to put a SIDC in front of it, and bundling a second copy in an app that already has one is how two versions of the icon set end up on one map. React is a peer for the usual reason — the core (src/core) has no React in it at all and can be used on its own, which is why the model and the component are separate entry points.
